title: Measure receipt-stream budget boundaries statically

identity.source_kind: git archive of exact commit; no Git metadata or runtime data

findings.claim: Write-count and source-stream byte budgets are independent. Ordinary JSONL has no total-size cap. Source-erasure uses expectedSize > 33554432 (equality completes). At default 32/run and 256/day, write-count binds first.
findings.evidence: static source plus executed createBudgetTracker and JSONL byte arithmetic in /work/out/boundary-fixture.ts

findings.claim: Exact 32 MiB complete/too-large and ordinary no-cap cases already exist. Exact write-count complete/too-large at the writer seam already exists. Do not duplicate those tests.
findings.evidence: static test/source agreement; tests themselves NOT_RUN in this container

findings.claim: A fresh in-memory tracker starts runUsed at 0, so a supplied day used==limit throws budget:canon_writes_per_day even when the run limit is 1. Run-first only after the run counter has already reached its cap.

Ordinary append can grow promotions.jsonl past 32 MiB. A later source-erasure open of the same file is then too-large. Daily budget accounting reads that log unbounded. Docs already call those readers separate work.
RFC 0002 names packages/core/test/loop/budget.test.ts, which is absent on this base. Current coverage is apply.test.ts and serve rail tests.
findings.evidence: packages/core/test/loop contains dedup-threshold.test.ts, self-ingest.test.ts, tri-state.test.ts only
